description: Held-out generalization corpus for the FIS False Critical Rate (FCR) benchmark. Purpose: the library-corpus 84%->100% clean-pass (commit a669e04) was produced by fixing the scanner IN RESPONSE to the same 25 repos it is scored on -- an in-sample tuning caveat METHODOLOGY.md flags as an outstanding v1 item. This corpus tests whether that fix GENERALIZES: these 9 repos were selected AFTER the scanner-precision fixes landed and were never run, inspected, or used to tune anything before being frozen here. They satisfy C1-C3 and C5-C7 of corpus.clean.json's predicates (see METHODOLOGY.md) and are absent from corpus.clean.json, corpus.app.json, corpus.vuln.json, and corpus.messy.json (checked against all four before freezing). C4 IS NOT FULLY SATISFIED -- see c4_shortfall below. This set also deliberately closes two disclosed selection-bias gaps in the original 25: it adds security-primitive/crypto libraries (jose, cryptography, golang-jwt/jwt) the original set had none of, and it caps JS/TS at 2/9 (22%) instead of the original's 52%, adding maintainers/orgs (expressjs, panva, pyca, encode, golang-jwt, labstack, tokio-rs, hyperium, rust-lang) with zero overlap with the sindresorhus/pallets/spf13 clusters already in corpus.clean.json.
metric: Same as corpus.clean.json: ideal verdict is production_ready or ready_with_conditions, ideal critical-finding count is 0. FCR (finding-level) = pure-model critical findings (repo has secretHits=0 AND vulnerableDeps=0) across the corpus. Report this held-out FCR separately from (never pooled with) the original 25's in-sample FCR -- pooling would re-contaminate the exact generalization question this corpus exists to answer.
c4_shortfall: DISCLOSED 2026-08-11 (adversarial re-check). Predicate C4 in METHODOLOGY.md is a MANIFEST-level check ('zero open critical/high CVEs in OSV at freeze date, verified via osv-scanner over each manifest'). The verification actually performed for this corpus was PACKAGE-level (OSV queried at each library's own latest published version), which is strictly weaker -- it asks whether the library itself has an advisory, never whether anything its manifest pins does. encode/httpx FAILS the manifest-level C4: its requirements.txt pins cryptography==45.0.7, which carries three HIGH advisories (GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5, GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf, GHSA-jwv3-5hgf-82ww). It was admitted because the weaker check passed it, and that admission produced the run's fourth not-green verdict, which an earlier METHODOLOGY draft then miscredited as a true positive. A manifest-level re-verification of all 9 entries is OUTSTANDING; until it is done, results on this corpus must not be cited as a full C1-C7 held-out result.
verification_note: Each entry verified live 2026-08-11 via the GitHub API (exists, not archived, language, star count, push recency) and via OSV.dev (queried at the exact latest published version per package -- zero applicable advisories at that version for all 9; NOTE this is the package-level check, weaker than predicate C4 as written -- see c4_shortfall) and via a live gitleaks 8.30.1 scan of a fresh shallow clone (predicate C5's non-FIS half; raw JSON reports in reports/fis/heldout-corpus-verification/). Four of the nine repos produced non-zero raw gitleaks hits; every hit was inspected and is a test-fixture/example/documentation key under a test/vectors/fixture/docs/cookbook path, not a committed production credential -- the same non-production-path standard corpus.app.json's curation rules already establish. This scanner run is independent evidence gathered for corpus construction; it is not, and should not be read as, a FIS engine run.
